question.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2\sqrt{2},-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ denotes the unit tangent vector.
question.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t),
$$

where the principal normal vector $N(t)$ is given by

$$
N(t)=\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{(0)^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{3}⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{(\frac{1}{3})}=⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the binormal vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2\sqrt{2},-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\times ⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2\sqrt{2} & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} & \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{2} & -\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 0 & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨({sin}^{2}⁡t-(-{cos}^{2}⁡t)),-(-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t-0),(-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-0)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨1,\,2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
